scenarios.description: Validate the drug-database uncertainty U001 (status unvalidated to validated).
scenarios.rationale: O8 blocking route: a validated uncertainty adds nothing to U_o, so the conditional guard no longer holds for R001 and R007. R001 keeps the soft rule C003 (governedBy I001, no validator), which yields a reservation, so accepted_with_reservations, matching the paper counterfactual. R007 has no soft rule applicable, so accepted. R002 lineage is G003 and G001 and it reads no element U001 touches, so unchanged.

scenarios.description: Change the impact level of U001 from high to low (blocking uncertainty, nearly unchanged).
scenarios.rationale: O8 blocking: an unvalidated uncertainty blocking L(G002) gives open regardless of impact level, so R001 and R007 stay conditional. U001 also affects G002, which is in the lineage of R001 and R007, so the affecting route applies, but low impact only adds a reservation that the open premise already dominates. No other requirement reads U001 or G002, so all ten decisions are unchanged.

scenarios.description: Add an unvalidated high-impact uncertainty U002 affecting the dosage property, and add requirement RX01 that maps like R003.
scenarios.add_turtle: ex:U002_DosageEstimate a reo:AssumptionUncertainty ; reo:uncertaintyId "U-002" ; reo:uncertaintyName "Dosage estimate" ; reo:impactLevel "high" ; reo:status "unvalidated" ; reo:affects ex:Prop_Dosage .
scenarios.add_requirements_turtle: req:RX01 a reo:Requirement ; reo:requirementId "RX01" ; reo:hasSeedGoal ex:G004 ; reo:assessedInContext ex:X001_EmergencyDept ; reo:hasResponsibleActor ex:Physician ; reo:performsAction ex:Action_Prescribe ; reo:requiresAuthorityOf ex:Physician ; reo:refersToConcept ex:D001_Medication ; reo:refersToProperty ex:Prop_Dosage .
scenarios.rationale: U002 affects Prop_Dosage, which is in refs(R003). O8 affecting route: unvalidated high gives open (U_o), no hard failure or unchecked, so R003 moves from accepted to conditional. RX01 has exactly the mapping of R003, so it gets the same decision. R006 also refers to Prop_Dosage but is already rejected by O2 and stays rejected. R001 and R007 are not affected because Prop_Dosage is not in their read sets.

scenarios.description: Remove the Medication exchange from interaction I002 (EHR to Pharmacist).
scenarios.rationale: O6 requires the used interaction to exchange a referenced concept. R004 and R005 refer to Medication (D001) and use I002, which now exchanges no concept, so O6 fails: hard failure, rejected. R005 was pending review before and is now rejected because H_f takes precedence over H_u. R010 uses I002 and was already rejected by O6. No other requirement uses I002.

scenarios.description: Detach uncertainty U001 from G002 by removing both its blocks and affects links.
scenarios.remove_turtle:
ex:U001_DrugDBFrequency reo:affects ex:G002 .
ex:U001_DrugDBFrequency reo:blocks ex:G002 .
scenarios.rationale: With no blocks or affects link, U001 is not in the read set of R001 or R007, so no O8 route fires. R001 keeps the soft rule C003, which has no validator and gives a reservation: accepted_with_reservations. R007 has no soft rule, so accepted. This shows that the decision depends on the links, not only on the status value.

scenarios.description: Remove the only authority level of the Physician.
scenarios.rationale: O3 requires the authority holder to exist and have an authority level, and failure is a hard failure. Every requirement with requiresAuthorityOf Physician (R001, R002, R003, R009; R008 already rejected) becomes rejected. The SHACL minimum-cardinality shape would flag the model, but the contract decides by O3 and the report is graph-level only. Requirements without requiresAuthorityOf Physician are unchanged.

scenarios.description: Remove the emergency-department exception of the HIPAA constraint C001.
scenarios.rationale: The antecedent of C001 is access_records, so C001 is triggered only for requirements that perform AccessRecords: R001, R002, R008. For them the consent-or-exception validator now fails (X001 is no longer an exception and asserts no consent), a hard failure, so R001 and R002 are rejected; R008 was already rejected. R004, R005, R007 and R010 have EHR_System or Physician in their applicable set but do not perform AccessRecords, so the rule is not triggered and they are unchanged.

scenarios.description: Raise the enforcement level of the response-time constraint C003 from soft to hard (no validator registered).
scenarios.rationale: C003 applies to requirements that use I001 (governedBy I001): R001, R002, R008. Hard and without a registered validator, it is unchecked and routed to H_u, so pending review. Pending review precedes conditional and accepted with reservations in the guard order. R008 stays rejected because C001 gives H_f. C003 has no antecedent, so it is always triggered. Other requirements do not use I001.

scenarios.description: Add a second, conflicting authority level for the Physician (resident_trainee).
scenarios.rationale: O9 forbids consulted elements with conflicting values, and the contract does not choose between the two authority levels (policy: pending review). Every requirement whose read set contains the Physician (R001, R002, R003, R009; R008 is already rejected) gets an H_u entry and so pending review, which overrides conditional. R004, R006, R007, R010 do not read the Physician, and R005 was already pending review.

scenarios.description: Remove EHR_System from the active actors of the emergency context and remove the Dispense capability of the Pharmacist.
scenarios.remove_turtle:
ex:X001_EmergencyDept reo:hasActiveActor ex:EHR_System .
ex:Pharmacist reo:hasCapability ex:Action_Dispense .
scenarios.rationale: O1: R007 is responsible for no goal in L(G002) = {G002, G001} and EHR_System is no longer active in X001, so O1 fails and R007 is rejected. R004 and R010 keep O1 because EHR_System is responsible for G005, their seed. O2: R005 performs Dispense, which the Pharmacist no longer holds, so R005 is rejected (H_f overrides its earlier pending review). Dispense is performed only by R005.

scenarios.description: Remove the type of goal G004 (so it is not an operational goal) and add two requirements with undefined or misplaced references.
scenarios.add_requirements_turtle:
req:RX02 a reo:Requirement ; reo:requirementId "RX02" ; reo:hasSeedGoal ex:G002 ; reo:assessedInContext ex:X001_EmergencyDept ; reo:hasResponsibleActor ex:Physician ; reo:performsAction ex:Action_Prescribe ; reo:requiresAuthorityOf ex:Physician ; reo:refersToConcept ex:D001_Medication ; reo:refersToProperty ex:Prop_PatientId .
req:RX03 a reo:Requirement ; reo:requirementId "RX03" ; reo:hasSeedGoal ex:G002 ; reo:assessedInContext ex:X001_EmergencyDept ; reo:hasResponsibleActor ex:Physician ; reo:performsAction ex:Action_Prescribe ; reo:requiresAuthorityOf ex:Physician ; reo:refersToConcept ex:D009_Unknown .
scenarios.rationale: Without the OperationalGoal type G004 is not in G, so the not-derived guard (s not in G) fires first for every requirement seeded at G004: R003, R006, R009. RX02 refers to Prop_PatientId, which Patient owns and Medication does not, so O5 fails: rejected. RX03 refers to the undefined concept D009_Unknown, so O4 fails: rejected. R001, R002 and R007 do not depend on G004 and are unchanged.

scenarios.description: Change the validation plan text of U001 (an attribute the contract never reads).
scenarios.rationale: validationPlan is not read by Algorithm 1 or any obligation. U001 is a touched identifier, so R001 and R007 are selected by DirectReEval, but their assessments are recomputed to the same values. Nothing else changes, so all ten decisions are unchanged.

cqs.question: Which actors are subject to the HIPAA constraint C001_HIPAA?
cqs.rationale: isSubjectTo is asserted directly in hospital.ttl for Physician and EHR_System. Pharmacist is subject only to C002 and C004, so it is not returned.

cqs.question: Which constraints are quality constraints, directly or through the subclass closure?
cqs.rationale: Only C003_ResponseTime is typed QualityConstraint in the extension. The zero-length rdfs:subClassOf* step includes the class itself, and no other class is a subclass of QualityConstraint.

cqs.question: Is there a hard-enforced constraint that has no validatorKey?
cqs.sparql: ASK { ?c reo:enforcementLevel 'hard' . FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?c reo:validatorKey ?k . } }
cqs.rationale: C004_DispensingLog is hard and carries no validatorKey, so the contract routes requirements that apply it to review. C001 and C002 both have validator keys.

cqs.question: Does any goal reach itself through a chain of refines links?
cqs.rationale: The refines links run from G002 to G005 up to G001, and G001 has no outgoing refines link, so there is no refinement cycle.

cqs.question: Which requirements have G002 as their seed goal?
cqs.rationale: In hospital-requirements.ttl only R001 and R007 have hasSeedGoal G002. Requirement IDs are plain literals compared by lexical form.

cqs.question: Which requirements declare a hard constraint?
cqs.rationale: Only R001 declares a hard constraint (C002_FDA) in the requirement file, so only R001 is returned.

cqs.question: Which goals are refined, directly or transitively, by G001?
cqs.rationale: G002 to G005 refine G001 directly. The transitive path adds nothing else because none of them has sub-goals, and G001 does not refine itself.

cqs.question: Which requirements have no derivation record in the snapshot?
cqs.sparql: SELECT ?id WHERE { ?r a reo:Requirement ; reo:requirementId ?id . FILTER NOT EXISTS { ?rec reo:assesses ?r . } }
cqs.rationale: The base snapshot contains no DerivationRecord instances, so all ten requirements lack a record. The query uses the assesses link that the spec uses for impact analysis, and avoids the prov prefix, which is not predefined.
